outcomes: A TypeScript workload that sets CONFIG_SERVER_URL boots on config and secrets resolved by Putnami Cloud, and a required source stops startup instead of running on partial config
A TypeScript workload publishes events through the managed Event Server with a short-lived token bound to the server audience, and no error message carries a token or provider text
nonGoals: Serving config, secrets or events: the Cloud server owns the endpoints this package calls
Parity with the Go runtime destination, which cloud/runtime/go owns

requirements.text: The remote config source resolves config from the server at CONFIG_SERVER_URL. A base URL receives a POST with a bearer token. An exact resolve URL receives a GET that keeps its query string. A 404 on that URL retries once against the CONFIG_SERVER_AUDIENCE origin. CONFIG_VERSION pins the resolve to a frozen version. The environment name goes out as configured.

eventServerDestination validates the whole managed binding before it asks for a credential, pins its route at construction, and refuses a stale topology generation before any token or network call. A publish sends the canonical JSON request with a bearer for the exact audience. A retry resends the same bytes with one credential. A cancelled or unavailable credential fails closed, and nothing is sent. Failures never carry token or provider text.

Event Server tokens are JWTs whose audience matches. The cache keeps one token per audience until shortly before expiry and shares one refresh across callers. A stuck provider times out with a redacted failure, and no second refresh starts while it is stuck. A malformed, expired or wrong-audience token is rejected. The Google source asks the metadata server for the exact audience and rejects an oversized response.

register adds the config and secrets source discoverers and forwards the cache-reset hooks. A base CONFIG_SERVER_URL enables both sources, at priority 50 and 55, between the .secrets file (35) and CONFIG_DATA (60). An exact resolve URL enables only the config source. An unset, blank, undefined or null URL enables none.

A required source retries a network failure until the server is ready, inside the retry budget. A terminal HTTP status such as 401 or 404 fails at once with no retry. A retry budget of 0 allows one attempt. CONFIG_SERVER_TIMEOUT sets the per-request timeout.

A source is required when K_SERVICE is set or NODE_ENV is production. When a required source fails, the load throws instead of falling back to local sources. A failed load during startup logs one structured JSON error line and exits with code 1.

The remote secrets source sends a POST to /api/secrets/resolve with a bearer token and the schema hash, at priority 55. An unresolved response yields no secrets. A source reuses its first resolve on later loads.

When a required config source exhausts its retries and a snapshot is configured, it boots on the snapshot and logs a warning. It never falls back after a 403 or resolved:false, and it prefers a config the server resolves. With no usable snapshot it throws. The snapshot loads once. The loader downloads the object from Cloud Storage and decrypts it with Cloud KMS.
The synchronous fetch the sources use at startup reuses one worker across small requests. A fetch that cannot complete throws.

An operator token from the environment wins over Google workload identity. Without one, K_SERVICE or GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT selects a Google metadata ID token for the CONFIG_SERVER_AUDIENCE or the server URL, cached within its lifetime. A failed metadata fetch yields no token. A configured token source wins over a static token. With no token, the request carries no Authorization header.
